correctness.rationale: Formal series identity \(F(q)/q=E(q^{24})P(q)P(q^3)^{-1}P(q^{12})^{-1}\), exact modulo-four linearization by divisor parity, and pentagonal-square change of exponent reconstruct the coefficient formula. At primes \(p\equiv1\pmod4\), cancellation of the three- and twelve-form pairs and unique odd-coordinate Gaussian representations prove the claim. For primes \(r\equiv11\pmod{12}\), both negative one and negative three are nonsquares, forcing even \(r\)-adic valuation of every representing form. All quantifiers are explicitly for positive indices and primes at least five. The standalone script independently checks 2000 coefficients, and each prime therein; finite checks support but do not imply infinite identities.

value.rationale: The congruence describes a naturally motivated number-theoretic partition statistic by explicit binary quadratic norms at every index. It classifies its prime-index residue completely, distinguishes prime classes with equal 1 mod 12 residue by an arithmetic Gaussian coordinate, supplies infinitely many provably nonzero instances, and gives a multiplicative inert-prime obstruction for composite indices. Earlier general lacunarity is acknowledged as previously known. This is a substantive structural congruence rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
